extracted.intended_audience: researchers and students preparing systematic reviews (health and social care)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for registering a systematic review protocol (primarily for PROSPERO and comparable registries), including what to prepare, timing, eligibility, and registry-selection considerations. Focus is on health- and social-care-related systematic reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register at inception / protocol stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Systematic reviews should be registered at inception (i.e. at the protocol stage) to help avoid unplanned duplication and to enable comparison of reported review methods with what was planned in the protocol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration at the protocol stage assists compliance with PRISMA and allows later comparison between the completed review and planned methods; PROSPERO records key protocol features as a permanent record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full protocol must be ready before registering
rubrics_metrics.description: A full protocol should be ready before registering with PROSPERO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare the complete protocol content before beginning registration so the registry record accurately reflects planned methods and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register before data extraction begins
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions must be made before data extraction commences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure registration occurs prior to extracting data to preserve the prospective nature of the registration and reduce risk of reporting bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration forms must be complete
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fill out all required fields on the registry form; incomplete submissions are not acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission language requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions must be in English (search strategies and protocols attached to a record may be in any language).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The main registration entry must be English-language to be accepted by PROSPERO, though you may attach searches/protocol documents in other languages.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROSPERO scope / eligibility (accepted topics)
rubrics_metrics.description: PROSPERO is an international database of prospectively registered systematic reviews in health and social care, welfare, public health, education, crime, justice, and international development, where there is a health related outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure your review addresses an outcome with clear relevance to human health to be within PROSPERO's remit; PROSPERO records key protocol features and maintains them as a permanent record.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROSPERO exclusion criteria (types of reviews not accepted)
rubrics_metrics.description: PROSPERO does not accept: systematic reviews without an outcome of clear relevance to the health of humans; scoping reviews; literature reviews that use a systematic search but not a systematic synthesis of the results or outcome; systematic reviews assessing sports performance as an outcome; methodological reviews that assess ONLY the quality of reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your review matches any of the excluded types, consider an alternative registry (e.g., OSF) or follow the appropriate publication route (e.g., Campbell Collaboration for social-policy evidence syntheses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not duplicate Cochrane protocol registrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Cochrane protocols are automatically uploaded — to avoid duplication of records, Cochrane protocols should not be registered separately with PROSPERO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your protocol is a Cochrane protocol, do not create a separate PROSPERO record; check the automatic upload process instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan sufficient time to complete PROSPERO registration
rubrics_metrics.description: The PROSPERO site indicates that 'most registrants complete the form in 60 minutes or less,' but that is very optimistic. Plan on giving yourself plenty of time to complete the registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow more than an hour to gather protocol details and fill in the registration form fully and accurately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose the appropriate registry for your review
rubrics_metrics.description: PROSPERO is for health- and social-care-related reviews with health outcomes; Campbell Collaboration supports high-quality, transparent evidence syntheses in the social sectors and publishes protocols; OSF Registries allows timestamped registrations and aggregation across registries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select a registry that matches your review's scope and goals (e.g., PROSPERO for health outcomes, Campbell for social-sector policy-relevant syntheses, OSF for broad timestamped registration and cross-registry discovery). Consider registered-report workflows (e.g., Campbell/Registered Reports) if publishing methods as a protocol is desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration benefits and purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Registering a systematic review provides benefits: provides a comprehensive listing of systematic reviews registered at inception; avoids duplication; counters publication bias; safeguards against reporting biases by revealing any differences between the methods or outcomes reported in the published review and those planned in the registered protocol; identifies whether there are any reviews already underway that address the topic of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use registration to increase transparency, to comply with journal/practice standards (e.g., PRISMA), and to inform stakeholders (peer reviewers, editors, funders, guideline developers, and the public) about planned reviews.
